name: Audrey Tang
description:
Civic hacker, co-author of «Plurality» (with Glen Weyl) and the forthcoming «Civic AI» (with Caroline Green). She is a Carnegie Distinguished Fellow at the Institute of Global Politics, Columbia SIPA and an inaugural Senior Accelerator Fellow at the Oxford Institute for Ethics in AI. 
She served as Taiwan's first Minister of Digital Affairs (2022–2024), preceded by six years as Minister without Portfolio for Digital Affairs (2016–2022), and is the world's first nonbinary cabinet minister. Tang was instrumental in the g0v (gov-zero) network and played a pivotal role in the 2014 Sunflower Movement, facilitating digital consensus-building during the occupation of Taiwan's legislature. As Digital Minister, she implemented radical transparency through participatory democracy platforms like vTaiwan and Join, with innovations such as the "Mask Map" during COVID-19 and defenses against cyber interference in the 2024 elections. 
In 2025, Tang received the Right Livelihood Award - often called the Alternative Nobel - "for advancing the social use of digital technology to empower citizens, renew democracy and heal divides."
